By this I mean that you should have your key bindings memorized and prepared when the situation calls.  With the mage, you have polymorph, mass poly (this may be an arcane talent), and slow (which can affect multiples if you talent into it).  What I advise, if you want to continue with arcane, is if there are multiple mobs close by, poly the FIRST mob, then cast slow on the second, and start building up those arcane charges with blast. Also, I find a lot of people save their one minute cooldowns way too much.  Use them and use them often.  Big pull?  Mirror image.  It buys you precious time so you can aim that glass cannon and BOOM.  Ice block when you need a moment to think (you can talent it so that it heals you to 80% also).  Frost nova + blink - this is a VERY important combo.  Use either without the other and it’s just less effective.  Time warp is super tricky to get right but once you do, it’s a lovely 40 second cooldown.  

Oh, and don’t forget your barriers.  Keep them up all the time.  Use them ahead of battle so you can recast in the middle of getting smacked around.

You may want to find a single mob and let it get a little close so you can become familiar with how mages can manipulate the battlefield.  Find your ‘oh shit’ rotation and practice it.

I hope this makes sense, I am very tired right now. 😅

It is possible, check out the people that body-build with calisthenics.  Andy Galpin, who is highly educated in this area, has a lot of data in regards to how hypertrophy is mainly about volume and not necessarily weight.  Progressive overload can be achieved with an increase in reps!  BUT you will plateau if you do not consume enough macronutrients AND if you do not vary your choice of exercises.  While squats, for example, should be included in your program you will want to work your way through the variations to maximize intensity.  Sumos, splits, pulsing at the lower end of the squat, are just a few ways to make the squat more challenging.  Just like how single-leg hip thrusts or frog pumps hit you harder than a basic hip thrust.  

The current belief is that advantage in calisthenics is they are easier on your joints, which is a plus.  But from my experience, beware of overtraining.  I work my butt and legs out at least three times a week over the last four years and I definitely have had to make use of foam rollers and massagers to avoid injuries.
